title: A few showers & thunderstorms Wednesday night, remaining seasonally mild | Weather | fox21online.com
text:
Wednesday was just the latest day for the Northland to see more hazy sunshine, warm summer temperatures, light winds, and slightly humid dew points. We should see a bit of a change in this pattern Wednesday night as the more active weather pattern that has stayed to our south will bump just enough north that those along and south of Highway 2 will have a widely scattered chance for showers and thunderstorms. Lows will remain seasonally mild in the 50s and low 60s. Thursday will see any precipitation move out, with a mix of sunshine and clouds to follow. Winds will remain light and dew points will remain a bit humid, with highs staying seasonally mild in the 70s and low 80s.
After a dry and breezy Friday, the Northland will see a stronger storm system push into the western Great Lakes region Friday night and Saturday. While it won’t be a washout, we should see a decent amount of rainfall in spots with highs in the 60s and 70s. The weekend will end with sunny conditions and seasonal temperatures. They will warm up again Monday back to the 80s, but the more active weather pattern will remain in the region. That will include a frontal system Tuesday, and another storm system later in the week.
Chief Meteorologist Rusty Mehlberg
